did_you_know.text: Psalm 124 opens with the title “A Song of Ascents. Of David,” and the speaker invites all Israel to affirm his words with “Let Israel now say.”
The word “Unless” opens the psalm and emphasizes that salvation depends on the LORD’s presence with Israel.
The danger is described as a person rising up against Israel; the psalm refers to the enemy in general terms and does not identify a specific foe here.
The enemies’ power is portrayed in an extreme image: they might swallow Israel alive, meaning destroy them completely.
From the third verse to the fourth, the imagery changes from a predator to rushing waters, conveying an overwhelming danger that is difficult to withstand.
The phrase “the raging waters” describes dangerous, turbulent waters; the repetition of “passed over our soul” intensifies the sense of threat.
After describing the danger, the psalm offers a blessing of thanksgiving: “Blessed be the LORD,” because He did not hand Israel over as prey to the enemies’ teeth.
The deliverance is compared to a bird escaping a hunter’s snare: the snare was broken, and the bird got away before it was caught.
The final verse summarizes the psalm with a declaration of faith: help comes “in the name of the LORD,” who is identified as the Maker of heaven and earth.
